piece.caption: How to secure business quotation data when using AI agents. When multiple AI agents pull rates from archived quotations or restricted pricing sheets, confidential terms can leak without human oversight. Securing your business data is not just about endpoint security, it requires complete data lineage to track how information is ingested, copied, and summarized across workflows. Have you audited which folders your AI tools can read?

claims.claim: AI agents pull data from multiple sources like restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes to draft proposals.
Without human checks during agent handoffs, unapproved confidential information can leak.
AI security in agentic workflows is primarily a data visibility problem rather than an application or endpoint tool problem.
Establishing data lineage tracks how data is ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, and redistributed across workflows.

piece.dm_text: Here is your 4-step Data Lineage Checklist for securing AI workflows: 1. Map Data Sources: Identify all databases, old quotations, and restricted pricing systems your AI agents can read. 2. Control Handoffs: Set strict permissions between multi-agent tasks to block unverified transfers. 3. Audit Data Movement: Track how data is continuously copied, summarized, and transformed by agents. 4. Enforce Human Gatekeeping: Ensure no automated draft containing sensitive rates reaches a client without human sign-off.

The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments.
The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments.
Jay Peters Nov 6, 2026, 12:37 AM UTC Link
Jay Peters is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme. Following this week’s midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion , OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won’t use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials.
Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing “only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.” In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies it works with on data center projects.
OpenAI’s additional commitments include paying “the full cost” of electricity it uses and the “infrastructure needed to serve us.” It will make opportunities for local communities by publishing the jobs it expects to create and by reporting on hiring. And every future “compute campus” (its rebranding phrase for data centers ) the company owns and operates will have a “local compact” that includes the commitments and will reflect “local priorities,” OpenAI says.

[52] MIT Tech Review AI — Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
URL: https://www.technologyreview.com/2026/11/04/1147596/securing-the-agentic-enterprise-with-data-lineage/
You need to enable JavaScript to view this site. Skip to Content Sponsored
A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents.
This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem.
Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient. Securing agentic AI at scale requires understanding how data moves. Teams, therefore, need to establish data lineage in order to effectively manage governance, accountability, and trust across human, agentic, and hybrid workflows.
